chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The jadh'ah (young sheep) is sufficient from the sheep, and from the goats, only the thani (second-year goat) is sufficient.'

key_terms.الثَّنِيُّ: A goat that has completed two years of age, valid for sacrifice.
key_terms.الضَّأْن: Sheep (specifically referring to the species in this context).
key_terms.الْجَذَعُ: A young sheep that has completed one year of age (entered its second year), valid for sacrifice.

ai.seo_question: What are the age requirements for sheep and goats to be valid for sacrifice (Qurbani) in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the distinct age criteria for valid sacrificial animals, reflecting the practical jurisprudence of the Imams regarding livestock maturity. It highlights the scholarly distinction between sheep (*dhanab*) and goats (*ma'z*), where the former requires only one year of age while the latter must be two years old, ensuring the animal is robust enough for the ritual. This ruling underscores the precision in Shia fiqh regarding the physical qualifications of the *udhiyah* to ensure the validity of the offering.
